problem:
The inverse of the matrix $A$ is found using the row operations as shown below. What are the corresponding row operations?

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

activity_context.topic_title: Finding the Inverse of a 2x2 Matrix Using Row Operations

examples.knowledge_point: Determining the Row Operations Required To Find the Inverse of a 2x2 Matrix
examples.problem:
The inverse of the matrix $A$ is found using row operations, as shown below. What are the row operations corresponding to each step?

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2} & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
examples.worked_solution:
We write down $A$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $A$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-3){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2} & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding row operations are

$$
R_1 := \dfrac{1}{2}R_1,
\qquad
R_1 := R_1+(-3)R_2.
$$

The matrix $A^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore,

feedback.problem:
The inverse of the $2\times 2$ matrix $Q$ is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine ${Q}^{-1}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}[Q\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \,4 & \,1 & 0 \\ 0 & \,-1 & \,-1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 &  &  \\ 0 & 1 &  & \end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
We write down $Q$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $Q$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[Q\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \,4 & \,1 & 0 \\ 0 & \,-1 & \,-1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-4){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix ${Q}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{Q}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 4 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$
